title: Common definitions (quant-fidelity-registry)
description: Shared $defs for every collection in the quantization-fidelity registry. Id shape and the huggingface_identity block are deliberately kept compatible with 0xSero/local-ai-registry so records can be cross-linked.

registry_id.description: Registry-local identifier. Same character class as local-ai-registry ids (lowercase, dot/hyphen, '--' segment separator) so ids remain cross-linkable. First segment is the collection tag: model--, artifact--, panel--, reference--, pipeline--, measurement--.

git_revision.description: A full or abbreviated git/HF commit sha. Abbreviated is tolerated but flagged by the validator when it is the ONLY identity a row has.

huggingface_identity.description: Structurally compatible with local-ai-registry common.schema.json#/$defs/huggingface_identity, plus a required-by-us 'revision' (a repo without a pinned revision is not an identity).

url.description: null only when link_type is 'none'. Some artifacts genuinely have no repository -- e.g. a serving-runtime configuration that was measured but never published as a checkpoint. Inventing a URL for one is worse than recording its absence.

path.description: Selector WITHIN the repository at that revision: a subfolder (orcarouter ships five builds as subfolders of one repo), a branch name (turboderp ships bpw variants as branches), or a single file (a .gguf). Repo+revision alone is not an identity when one repo holds several artifacts.

allOf.description: No repository link means no URL to give.

attribution.description: WHO is responsible for a thing. Never inferred; if unknown say so explicitly.

handle.description: HF username / GitHub handle, no email addresses.

is_registry_maintainer.description: true only for malaiwah. Used by the validator to decide whether a row may claim measured_by=self-measured.

source.description: A pointer to evidence. A source with kind=receipt_file/hf_file/github_file SHOULD carry a sha256; self-measured rows MUST have at least one such source with a sha256. A source cited for a PROVENANCE ASSERTION (disclosure.asserts_provenance) must additionally be PINNED -- a commit sha in the path, or a revision, or a sha256 -- because a claim anchored to a moving branch stops being provenance the moment somebody pushes.

lines.description: Optional line anchor into the pinned file, e.g. "373-378" or "210". Only meaningful with a COMMIT-pinned uri: line numbers move, so an anchor against a branch is worse than no anchor at all.

disclosure.description: One deviation, caveat or known defect. The array that holds these is REQUIRED and non-empty everywhere it appears; a record with nothing to disclose must say so with code=no_known_deviations. A disclosure that ASSERTS PROVENANCE must say so and must cite pinned evidence: an assertion is a published claim exactly as much as a metric is, and until PROV-014 only the metric needed a receipt.

code.description: Stable machine code, e.g. no_known_deviations, cross_stack_capture, unsealed_source, reduced_run_count, undisclosed_panel, different_reference_kind, author_reported_only, revision_unpinned, subset_of_panel, tp_sliced_artifact.

affects_comparability.description: true when this disclosure means the row must not be silently ranked against same-panel rows.

asserts_provenance.description: true when this disclosure makes a claim about HOW the artifact was produced or WHERE it came from -- a mechanism, a lineage, a code path, an inherited config -- rather than only describing the record. A true here obliges `sources` (invariant PROV-014).

sources.description: Evidence for THIS disclosure's claim, not for the record as a whole. Required when asserts_provenance is true, and every entry must be pinned (PROV-015).

cross_refs.description: Links out to other registries. Kept open so more registries can be added without a schema bump.

tensor_class.description: Coarse, model-agnostic weight class. 'other' requires a note in the enclosing entry.

harness.description: WHICH CODE PRODUCED THIS NUMBER. Additive and mandatory going forward: a row whose id is not in schema/harness-grandfather.json must carry a recorded harness covering metric.value (HARN-001). The identity is the CONTENT DIGEST SET of the computational closure -- every file on the path from the published inputs to the published number, enumerated by role -- plus the tool versions, and NOT the repository commit (which changes on a docs edit) and NOT the whole tree (same reason). The guarantee is one-way: equal harness_id means identical code; a differing id means read code_digests, because the boundary errs deliberately toward over-sensitivity. See registry/tools/harness_id.py, which is the implementation and carries the reasoning.

harness_id.description: 'harness--' + sha256(canonical_json({boundary, code_digests, tool_versions}))[:16]. Recomputed by the validator (HARN-003), never trusted. null exactly when recorded is false.

recorded.description: false is the honest shape for a row measured before this mechanism existed. It is NOT an invitation to reconstruct digests from today's checkout: those files are not the files that produced the row, and a plausible digest set would be a fabricated provenance record.

boundary.description: Named digest-set boundary, e.g. estimator_closure/v1. Two rows are only code-comparable within one boundary.

covers.description: Which parts of THIS row the stamp attests. A row whose headline came from a GPU run that predates the mechanism but whose intervals were re-derived locally covers uncertainty and by_domain and NOT metric.value -- claiming otherwise would be the exact failure this block exists to prevent.

commit_role.description: 'exact': the named commit's tree holds these exact closure bytes, verified file by file. 'parent': the number was produced by an uncommitted working tree, so the honest pointer is the commit it was based on -- a change cannot contain its own sha. Under 'parent' the code_digests, not the commit, are the identity.

dirty.description: true when the CLOSURE FILES differed from `commit` -- the closure, not the whole worktree, because a reseed necessarily changes data/ and that says nothing about which code ran. Always true under commit_role=parent.

repository.description: A human pointer, deliberately NOT an input to harness_id.

path.description: Repository-relative. Never absolute: a published receipt once pointed at /home/jl_fs on a filesystem that no longer exists.

tool_versions.description: python/numpy/torch and anything else whose version can move a number. This one DOES enter harness_id: CPython 3.12 switched builtin sum() to Neumaier summation and moved this project's reductions in the last ULP, so an interpreter is part of the estimator.

coverage_measured.description: What this interval's coverage MEASURES, against what it CLAIMS. Published because a nominal level is a property of the method's asymptotics and this panel is not asymptotic: g runs 5-7 per domain.

population.description: The known-truth distribution the coverage was measured against, e.g. 'lognormal fitted to this cell's own window means'.

miss_low.description: Fraction of reps where TRUTH fell ABOVE the interval, i.e. the interval understated divergence. Reported separately because undercoverage in this direction is the harmful one.

source.description: The simulation that produced these numbers.
